sshPushWorkflow.description: Pushes config over an interactive SSH shell (ssh2 Client), not NETCONF — same mechanism as the DIA generators (see dia-service-templates.xml).
sshPushWorkflow.step: Enter a private candidate config session.
Write each generated "set ..." command line-by-line to the shell stream.
Validate the candidate config without committing.
Commit only after commit check succeeds; exits config mode afterward.
sshPushWorkflow.errorTrigger: Any of these substrings in accumulated stdout aborts the push and rejects the promise.

circuitIdConvention.description: Only derives the l2circuit virtual-circuit-id (vcId) — GPON has NO description-flavored CID transform (contrast with DIA's cidForDescription/"LTZ" logic). The customer's account number (e.g. "LHTZ-6779") is an entirely independent input field, not derived from the CID.

rule.input: Any CID string; non-digit characters are stripped first.

descriptionTagFormat.description: Interface descriptions use an angle-bracket flavor, distinct from DIA's brace-delimited flavor. Do not mix the two within this service.
descriptionTagFormat.example: << cat=GPON|nbr=LTZ-ACC1-ITO ge-0/0/27| LYNY SUPPLY AND SERVICES | LHTZ-6779>>
descriptionTagFormat.note: The parent ps/physical interface gets the simple interfaceTagPattern; only the unit gets the full metadata tag.

l2circuitPattern.description: Delivered as an MPLS L2 circuit (pseudowire) between the Access Switch and a BNG, configured symmetrically via `set protocols l2circuit neighbor <peer-ip> interface <local-intf> ...`. Common leaf statements: virtual-circuit-id, control-word, mtu, pseudowire-status-tlv. Unlike DIA With Tag, the BNG-facing leg of the pseudowire is untagged, so encapsulation-type there is "ethernet" (not "ethernet-vlan") and appears only on the Access Switch end.

redundancyPattern.description: bngDevices is an array of 2 ([primary, backup]) — validate length >= 2. Unlike DIA (where backup-neighbor lives on the Metro/access side pointing toward the PE/BNG — same placement concept here), GPON's `backup-neighbor` is configured on the ACCESS SWITCH side only, pointing at the backup BNG. The BNG side's l2circuit always targets the single Access Switch and never carries backup-neighbor itself, since each BNG only needs one path to that access switch.

serviceType.name: GPON over Enterprise
serviceType.description: Enterprise circuit delivered over a shared GPON access network. An Access Switch (physical port, one VLAN unit per customer) is transported via l2circuit to a BNG's ps interface, which uses dynamic/auto-configured stacked VLAN ranges (subscriber-management style) rather than a single static VLAN unit — so, unlike DIA With Tag's Metro side, there is no separate "shared port" command variant needed here: the BNG ps interface commands are identical regardless of how many customers use that BNG, because VLAN handling is delegated to the dynamic-profile/access-profile subscriber logic rather than to individually-declared static units.

parameter.name: vlanId
parameter.note: Also used as the Access Switch's unit number.

parameter.name: accountNumber
parameter.note: Independent input field — NOT derived from cid.

parameter.name: cid
parameter.note: Only used to derive vcId; no description-flavored transform.

device.label: BNG (ps interface)
device.note: Same command set pushed to BOTH primary and backup BNG. No port-sharing variant — commands are identical every time.
device.commandTemplate: set interfaces ps{psUnit} description "<< {accountName} >>"
set interfaces ps{psUnit} anchor-point {anchorPoint}
set interfaces ps{psUnit} flexible-vlan-tagging
set interfaces ps{psUnit} auto-configure stacked-vlan-ranges dynamic-profile {profilePrefix}-GPON-VLAN-PROFILE accept any
set interfaces ps{psUnit} auto-configure stacked-vlan-ranges dynamic-profile {profilePrefix}-GPON-VLAN-PROFILE ranges any,any
set interfaces ps{psUnit} auto-configure stacked-vlan-ranges access-profile {profilePrefix}-GPON
set interfaces ps{psUnit} mtu {mtu}
set interfaces ps{psUnit} unit 0 description "<< cat=GPON|nbr={accessSwitchName} {accessIntf}| {accountName} | {accountNumber}>>"
set interfaces ps{psUnit} unit 0 encapsulation ethernet-ccc
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {accessSwitchIp} interface ps{psUnit}.0 virtual-circuit-id {vcId}
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {accessSwitchIp} interface ps{psUnit}.0 control-word
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {accessSwitchIp} interface ps{psUnit}.0 mtu {mtu}
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {accessSwitchIp} interface ps{psUnit}.0 no-vlan-id-validate
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {accessSwitchIp} interface ps{psUnit}.0 pseudowire-status-tlv
device.note: No backup-neighbor here — BNG's l2circuit always points at the single Access Switch; redundancy is expressed on the Access Switch side instead. No encapsulation-type ethernet-vlan either, since the BNG-facing leg is not itself VLAN tagged (tagging/detagging happens via the dynamic-profile subscriber logic).

device.label: Access Switch (physical interface)
device.commandTemplate: set interfaces {accessIntf} description "{accountName} | {accountNumber}"
set interfaces {accessIntf} flexible-vlan-tagging
set interfaces {accessIntf} speed auto
set interfaces {accessIntf} mtu 9000
set interfaces {accessIntf} encapsulation flexible-ethernet-services
set interfaces {accessIntf} gigether-options auto-negotiation
set interfaces {accessIntf} unit {vlanId} description "<< GPON | {accountName} | {accountNumber} >>"
set interfaces {accessIntf} unit {vlanId} encapsulation vlan-ccc
set interfaces {accessIntf} unit {vlanId} vlan-id {vlanId}
set interfaces {accessIntf} unit {vlanId} input-vlan-map push
set interfaces {accessIntf} unit {vlanId} input-vlan-map vlan-id {vlanId}
set interfaces {accessIntf} unit {vlanId} output-vlan-map pop
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {primaryBngIp} interface {accessIntf}.{vlanId} virtual-circuit-id {vcId}
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {primaryBngIp} interface {accessIntf}.{vlanId} control-word
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {primaryBngIp} interface {accessIntf}.{vlanId} mtu {mtu}
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {primaryBngIp} interface {accessIntf}.{vlanId} encapsulation-type ethernet
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {primaryBngIp} interface {accessIntf}.{vlanId} pseudowire-status-tlv
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {primaryBngIp} interface {accessIntf}.{vlanId} backup-neighbor {backupBngIp} virtual-circuit-id {vcId}
device.note: input-vlan-map push / output-vlan-map pop performs VLAN tag imposition/removal at the access edge (push on ingress toward the core, pop on egress toward the customer) — this is how a single-tagged customer port maps onto the untagged ethernet-ccc pseudowire on the BNG side. encapsulation-type here is "ethernet" (untagged far-end), contrasting with DIA With Tag's "ethernet-vlan". This device builder currently issues the physical interface-level commands (1-6) every time, with no shared-port variant like dia-with-tag's Metro switch — each Access Switch port in this generator is assumed dedicated to one customer's VLAN unit namespace at a time. If multi-customer sharing of one Access Switch port is later needed, model it the same way dia-with-tag splits dedicated-port vs shared-port commands.

relationToDiaFamily.description: See dia-service-templates.xml for the DIA No Tag / DIA With Tag services. Key structural differences from that family:

axis.name: routed customer IP / policer / BGP route-filter

relationToDiaFamily.axis: GPON has none — pure L2, no family inet anywhere.
GPON has none; uses an independent accountNumber field instead of DIA's LTZ-prefixed cidForDescription.
GPON uses angle-bracket << ... >> tags; DIA uses brace-delimited {...} tags.

GPON places it on the Access Switch (equivalent role to DIA's Metro switch) — same conceptual side as DIA, but note GPON's BNG-facing leg has no VLAN tagging at all, whereas DIA With Tag's PE-facing leg is tagged.
GPON's BNG side uses dynamic/subscriber auto-configure stacked-vlan-ranges instead of a single static VLAN unit — no equivalent in either DIA variant.

newServiceChecklist.item: If the new service is pure L2 (no customer-routed IP), follow this file's pattern rather than DIA's routed pattern.

If BNG/PE-side VLAN assignment should be dynamic per-subscriber rather than a static per-customer unit, model it on the auto-configure stacked-vlan-ranges + dynamic-profile/access-profile pattern here.

Decide independently whether the CID needs a description-flavored transform (DIA-style) or whether a separate account-number field is more appropriate (GPON-style) — do not assume one applies to the other.

If the access-facing physical port may need to be shared across multiple customers (as dia-with-tag's Metro side can), split the physical interface-level commands from the per-customer unit/l2circuit commands the same way dia-with-tag's portVariants does — this generator does not currently do that.
Follow the same SSH push workflow (configure private → commit check → commit and-quit) and expose both a push* (executes) and preview* (dry run) function, matching the existing module.exports shape.
